title: NEVER HUNG
author: Ensemble
question: Missing Data Art (seed-20260907-220129-aa5f, seeded 2026-09-07)
medium: One self-contained HTML surface, offline, one file, no library, no external asset, and no network request of any kind. An exhibition of twenty-five works this practice decided not to make, in the order they died. They hang as empty frames on one hanging line, along a wall that scrolls: the area of every frame is exactly proportional to the number of words this practice wrote about that work, so the wall is a skyline of paperwork about things that do not exist. The frames stay empty — nothing here reconstructs what a killed work would have looked like, because inventing the thing whose absence is the subject is the one move this work may not make. One press fills each frame instead with the only body these works have: their surviving documents, as bands whose heights are the share of the record each document is, tiling the frame exactly, with the entry in the practice's register of refusals as the coloured band at the bottom. Below the wall is the catalogue: for every work, what it would have been, the dated sentence that killed it quoted from this practice's own record, the register's entry or its silence, and every surviving path with its word count. Without a script a reader loses only the fill: the whole wall, the whole catalogue and every verdict are in the served document.
embodies: A CATALOGUE OF DATA ART IS A SURVIVORSHIP RECORD. It holds what was made; it cannot hold what was refused, because nobody writes down a work that does not exist. This practice does write them down, and so it can hang its own refusals: 25 works, 286 662 words of surviving record, 108 documents, and not one object. THE MEASURE IS THE POINT: frame area is words written, so the largest frame on the wall (STOP USING IMMEDIATELY, 63 239 words) is the work with the longest paperwork and not the best one, and the smallest (THE QUIET SIGNATURE, 30 words) is a paragraph in a register. Both are equally unmade. AND THE WORK FOUND A HOLE IN ITS OWN SOURCE. The register of refusals held twenty entries and its last was written on 2026-08-16 — but four concepts died after that date (INGRESS 08-16, UNISON 08-18, TENANCY 08-20, SILENT PERIOD 08-21) and not one was ever entered. They were written up on the live working board, which was retired to the archive on 2026-08-30 under a new constitution; the same session wrote this practice's closing report, which told its readers that twenty proposals were killed and named its source in its own footnotes as the twenty dated entries in the register. So the account of what this practice had refused was itself missing four refusals, and the number twenty has stood in this repository since. It is twenty-four. The register was repaired on the night this work was built — 752 words in four late entries, dated at the killings, with nothing above them edited and the closing report left standing as published — and those words are counted nowhere on the wall, because four frames here are the size of a record that did not exist. THE LAST FRAME IS NOT A KILL. OUTSTANDING survived this practice's gate, ran eight sessions in production and was held on one thing that was never this practice's to give; then the constitution it belonged to was replaced. It was never refused and has never been shown. A work can go missing without anyone deciding anything.
form: An exhibition: a wall, a hanging line, numbered frames, a printed catalogue.
form_argument: The house's direction of 2026-09-07 asks for a work that answers named Atlas works. The nearest of them is a filing cabinet of empty folders, and the risk of answering it in a browser is that empty frames are empty folders with a new medium — the copy the direction forbids. Three things make this a different object. (1) EVERY ABSENCE HERE HAS AN AUTHOR, a date and a written reason, quoted and checkable: it is a register of decisions, not of neglect. (2) THE ABSENCES ARE MEASURED. A folder has no size; a refusal here is the size of the paperwork it produced, which is a real quantity nobody had computed and which orders the room. (3) THE WORK ACTS ON ITS OWN SOURCE: it found the register four short and repaired it in the same commit, which a cabinet cannot do. The hanging line is the museum convention of hanging every work on one centre line, and it does the figure's work: with areas proportional and centres fixed, the eye reads the record as a skyline. Numbers under the frames rather than plaques, because at these sizes a plaque is unreadable and a numbered wall with a catalogue in the hand is how a hang is actually read — and because the wall is meant to give a visitor nothing but empty rectangles until they go looking.

in_atlas: The Library of Missing Datasets (v2.0) — Mimi Ọnụọha, 2016–2018. Looked at on 2026-09-08 at its gallery page: a powder-coated steel filing cabinet, 22.5 × 20 × 16 in, of empty folders each labelled with a dataset that does not exist, drawn from a list kept since 2015; six photographs of the cabinet and its interior; the page notes the colour of the cabinet 'speaks as much to value as to realities of wealth extraction'. DAYLIGHT: her absences have no author — nobody decided not to collect that data, and the structural nature of the not-collecting is her point. Every absence on this wall was decided, by this practice, on a named night, with a written reason a stranger can read and overrule; and each is the size of the paperwork the decision produced.

Missing Datasets (list/essay) — Mimi Onuoha, 2015–ongoing. Looked at on 2026-09-08 at its repository: the public list behind the cabinet, framing missing datasets as blank spaces in otherwise data-saturated environments, opening with 'the word missing is inherently normative. It implies both a lack and an ought', and giving four reasons datasets go uncollected, the first being that those with the resources to collect lack the incentive. DAYLIGHT: her reasons are incentives; ours are verdicts, dated and signed. LICENCE: the repository states no licence, so nothing from it is embedded here — it is named, linked and quoted only in short.

Biblioteca de la No-Historia — Voluspa Jarpa, 2011. A thousand hand-bound books reproducing declassified state files with their seals, stamps and redaction blackouts kept as the material. DAYLIGHT: her hole was cut into a record by a censor; the hole this work found was made by nobody at all — no one struck the four missing entries out, the keeping simply stopped, and an unkept register loses exactly as much as a redacted one.
outside_atlas: Unbuilt Roads: 107 Unrealized Projects — Hans Ulrich Obrist and Guy Tortosa, Hatje Cantz, 1997. Collects other artists' unrealised projects as proposals, in their authors' own descriptions, mostly unrealised for external reasons. DAYLIGHT: this is one practice's refusals of itself, each carrying the verdict that killed it, and measured rather than described.

This practice's own closing report, 2026-08-30 (closing-report/index.html) — the nearest neighbour of all, in this same repository: it tabulated twenty of these kills in prose with a Why column. DAYLIGHT: it is a text about the practice; this is an exhibition of the works, measured, exhaustive at twenty-four, and it is also the document that corrects the report's count.

licence.note: No third-party code is embedded in the page or in the tools that made it — no library, no external asset, and the page makes no network request of any kind. Under the licence rule of the direction of 2026-09-03: Mimi Onuoha's missing-datasets repository states no licence, so it is read, linked and named as a neighbour and nothing from it is embedded. A browser automation tool was used for headless verification only and is not a dependency of the work.

verification.build: build.py derives every number on the page from files in this repository. It fails the build if a manifest path does not exist, if any file is assigned to two works, or if any of the 25 quoted verdicts is not found in the file it is attributed to (whitespace-collapsed, byte-exact otherwise). --check rebuilds and fails on a one-byte drift: data.json and index.html are byte-identical on rebuild.
verification.browser: verify.mjs, 46 checks in a real browser with scripting off and on. Without script: all 25 frames, all 25 catalogue entries, every title, verdict, description and cited path in the served document; the fill control hidden because it cannot work; no horizontal page overflow at 1280 or 390. With script: no console errors, NO NETWORK REQUEST OF ANY KIND, frame area proportional to words across all 25 frames to within 0.2 %, every frame centred on the hanging line to within 0.01 px, and every filled frame's bands in the exact proportions of its documents, tiling the frame with nothing left over. Dark mode and the phone scale are checked as measurements, not as impressions.
verification.record: The four late entries appended to memory/discarded.md tonight are measured and printed but counted in no frame; verify.mjs checks that no frame's total includes a word written tonight.

video.note: HEYGEN_API_KEY was checked in this session's environment at open and is not present — the sixth night running. No avatar video was planned, attempted or generated; no minute was spent.

known_limits: Words are a proxy for effort and a poor one: a long ruling is not a long night.

Two of the twenty-five had bodies that were actually built (One Tap, premiered and withdrawn; Stop Using Immediately, one built page never published). This wall measures the record of their killing, not those bodies, which are kept elsewhere in the repository and named in the catalogue.

Which works are on the wall and which documents belong to each are judgments, written by hand in manifest.py. What would show the work wrong is a work this practice decided not to make that is not on this wall.
The deepest absence is not on the wall at all: the works nobody proposed. A register can only hold what somebody thought of.
